question: Does a very-low-cost LLM identify actionable semantic information in listing copy that is incremental to deterministic rules?
hypothesis: On a controlled 100-record stress test, gpt-5-nano can identify residual cross-field semantic issues or reusable rule candidates beyond literal rule-based checks while maintaining low false-positive behavior on clean controls.
primary_change: add an LLM residual semantic audit after deterministic rule extraction

scoring_time.timestamp_definition: listing copy and structured attributes available on the spot record; no future inquiry or outcome data is sent

population.eligibility: 100 deterministic records across rules-positive, Land semantic residual, ambiguity challenge, and clean-control strata
exclusions: pricing/geography fields irrelevant to semantic QA
catalog-wide API execution before pilot review

removed: LLM extraction of claims already available through rules

validation.strategy: 100-record balanced stress test before any scale-up
validation.split_description: 25 rules-positive, 25 Land semantic residual, 25 ambiguity challenge, 25 clean controls. This sample evaluates incremental semantics and false positives; it is not a prevalence sample.

items.evidence: Only current listing text and structured listing attributes are sent.
No inquiry, response, conversion, or future outcome information is part of the LLM payload.
